It treats changes in Identifier's own differential and local element definitions as in scope. Changes inherited only from `Element`, the new `DataType` base, `Extension`, primitive datatypes, `Reference`, `Period`, `CodeableConcept`, or target resource definitions are not emitted as local findings.

General changes to primitive datatypes (`uri`, `string`, `code`), complex datatypes (`CodeableConcept`, `Period`, `Reference`), and the `Organization` reference target resource are delegated to their own artifact reports.

narrativeReportMd:
# Identifier R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard structural instance-breaking changes were found for the local `Identifier` datatype: the local element set, cardinalities, datatypes, reference target for `assigner`, modifier flag, and summary flags are stable. The main migration issues are semantic and conformance-oriented: R6 adds an Identifier-specific warning invariant requiring `value.exists()`, sharpens `Identifier.system` from a namespace URL to an absolute URL with registry guidance, and updates the required `Identifier.use` binding version with a changed definition for `usual`.

## Scope
The analysis is scoped to the base `Identifier` datatype. Inherited/base changes such as the new `DataType` base class and inherited `Element`/`Extension` constraint propagation are not counted as Identifier findings.

## Main migration themes
Existing R4 data with `Identifier` instances that omit `value` can remain structurally valid in R6 but will now produce a warning. Implementers that used local or relative strings in `Identifier.system` should review them because R6's text now says the namespace is an absolute URL and points to registry rules for known identifier systems. Systems that interpret `Identifier.use = usual` should review display-selection logic because R6 narrows the definition to cases where the display/use identifier differs from the official identifier.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest impact is the `Identifier.system` semantic narrowing because non-canonical identifier namespaces can undermine matching, deduplication, and interoperability even when schema validation passes. The `ident-1` warning is lower impact for exchange validity but can break CI gates or operational validation policies that treat warnings as failures.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for deciding whether existing relative/local identifier systems can be migrated to stable absolute URLs and for interpreting the referenced identifier registry rules.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 changes mostly clarify conformance rather than restructure data. The new warning invariant could have been published only as prose or best-practice guidance, but an explicit warning gives validators a consistent signal without making old instances invalid. The absolute-URL language is interoperably useful but may expose old local practices that were tolerated by weak validation.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should handle the R6 `DataType` base introduction and any external terminology changes in THO v2-0203 used by `Identifier.type`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Identifier` has no local structural R4-to-R6 break, but it does have conformance and semantic changes. Top concerns are the new `ident-1` warning for missing `value`, the stronger absolute-URL/registry language for `system`, and the changed meaning of `Identifier.use` code `usual`. The biggest uncertainty is how strictly local validators and trading partners will enforce the prose around identifier systems and external terminology versions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should focus on data quality rather than reshaping JSON/XML. Audit Identifier instances with no `value`, audit `system` values for absolute canonical URLs and registry alignment, and review business logic that treats `usual` as simply the preferred display identifier. No transform is needed for cardinality, element names, local datatypes, or `assigner` references.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition-level facts because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and their local elements compared directly. Confidence is medium for terminology semantics outside `Identifier.use` because R6 does not include the external THO v2-0203 CodeSystem in the core package, and no official diff or full narrative registry page was available locally.

findings.title: R6 adds a warning invariant for Identifier instances with no value

oldState.summary: R4 had no Identifier-specific invariant requiring or warning on value presence.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

semanticText.definition: An identifier - identifies some entity uniquely and unambiguously. Typically this is used for business identifiers.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, an `Identifier` with `system`, `type`, `period`, `assigner`, extensions, or even only inherited content could satisfy base element rules without any Identifier-specific warning about an absent `value`.

newState.summary: R6 adds local warning invariant `ident-1` with expression `value.exists()`.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

Identifier with no value has limited utility.  If communicating that an identifier value has been suppressed or missing, the value element SHOULD be present with an extension indicating the missing semantic - e.g. data-absent-reason

semanticText.comment: The rules of the identifier.type  determine if a check digit is part of the ID value or sent separately, such as through the checkDigit extension.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 still keeps `Identifier.value` optional (`0..1`), but a base `Identifier` instance without a `value` now triggers a warning. The invariant is local to Identifier and appears in the R6 differential.

facts.note: R6 links the warning condition to `Identifier.value`; this does not change the element's cardinality.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The finding compares the same root element id `Identifier` and the same child element `Identifier.value` across both snapshots and differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard validation break because the new invariant has severity `warning`, not `error`, and `Identifier.value` remains optional. It can still be operationally breaking for pipelines that fail on warnings or for quality gates that previously accepted Identifier fragments with no value silently. The warning also changes migration expectations for suppressed or unknown identifier values: the R6 text says the `value` element should be present with an extension such as data-absent-reason to communicate the missing-value semantic.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Identifiers without values can cause matching, audit, and deduplication errors; R6 surfaces that risk as a warning rather than invalidating the instance.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve data quality by warning that an Identifier without `value` is usually not useful and should make absent-value semantics explicit.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use base narrative guidance instead of adding the `ident-1` warning invariant to the base snapshot.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: an `Identifier` without `value` is often unsafe for matching and should make missing or suppressed value semantics explicit. R6 uses warning severity and keeps `Identifier.value` optional, so most R4 instances remain structurally valid; the practical break is limited to validators or workflows that treat warnings as failures. A less-disruptive design exists, but it only partially meets the goal because it would not give base validators a consistent computable signal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep the R4 shape and cardinality and place the absent-value advice only in the Identifier definition/comment, without a base invariant. That would preserve validator behavior for all R4-valid value-less identifiers. The tradeoff is material: the quality rule would become prose that automated validators may ignore, and systems could continue exchanging identifiers whose missing-value semantics are ambiguous.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids new validator warnings but loses a uniform automated signal for value-less identifiers.

evidence.detail: R4 root Identifier has only inherited `ele-1` in the local snapshot.
R6 adds local warning invariant `ident-1` with expression `value.exists()`.
evidence.quote: Identifier with no value has limited utility.

evidence.detail: R6 links `Identifier.value` to condition `ident-1` while keeping cardinality `0..1`.

examples.examplesMd: The first fragment is illustrative of a value-less Identifier that can remain structurally valid but now triggers the R6 warning. The migration fragment shows the R6-recommended pattern of making the `value` element present with a missing-value extension when the actual value is suppressed or absent.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a local warning invariant, `ident-1`, to the root `Identifier`: `value.exists()`. This does not make `value` mandatory and therefore is not a hard instance break. It does change validator output and conformance expectations for any system that sends Identifier instances as placeholders, with only `system`, only `assigner`, only `type`, or with a suppressed value represented only outside `value`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance without `Identifier.value` is not automatically invalid in R6, but an R6 validator that reports warnings will now flag it. Strict CI or import policies that escalate warnings to failures can experience runtime or workflow breaks. R6 content that uses `_value.extension` to explain the absent value is structurally representable in R4 if the extension is accepted, but systems must not assume the identifier can be used for matching without an actual value.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit Identifier instances with missing `value`. If the value is truly unknown, suppressed, or masked, consider representing that explicitly on the `value` primitive element with a data-absent-reason-style extension and document downstream matching behavior. Test validators and ingestion pipelines with warning handling enabled so warning-as-error policies are discovered before production migration.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the change is a warning rather than an error, it is a backward-compatible way to signal a quality issue while preserving exchange of legacy data. A fully backward-compatible alternative would be prose-only guidance, but that would not give automated validators a consistent signal.

findings.title: Identifier.system semantics now explicitly require an absolute URL and refer to registry rules

oldState.summary: R4 described `Identifier.system` as a URL namespace for the identifier value.

semanticText.definition: Establishes the namespace for the value - that is, a URL that describes a set values that are unique.
semanticText.requirements: There are many sets  of identifiers.  To perform matching of two identifiers, we need to know what set we're dealing with. The system identifies a particular set of unique identifiers.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 already expected a URL-like namespace, but the local StructureDefinition text did not say `absolute URL` and did not include the new registry SHALL guidance.

newState.summary: R6 describes `Identifier.system` as an absolute URL and adds registry guidance for certain identifier types.

semanticText.definition: Establishes the namespace for the value - that is, an absolute URL that describes a set values that are unique.
semanticText.comment: Identifier.system is always case sensitive. The FHIR specification, terminology.hl7.org and HL7 affiliates (for identifiers specific to their jurisdiction) define identifier systems that SHALL be used for certain types of identifiers.  Specific rules can be found [here](identifier-registry.html).
semanticText.requirements: There are many sets  of identifiers.  To perform matching of two identifiers, we need to know what set we're dealing with. The system identifies a particular set of unique identifiers.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same optional `uri` datatype but strengthens the semantic text by explicitly saying the namespace is an absolute URL and by adding a SHALL-level pointer to registered systems for certain identifier types.

facts.oldValue: a URL that describes a set values that are unique
facts.newValue: an absolute URL that describes a set values that are unique
Identifier.system is always case sensitive. The FHIR specification, terminology.hl7.org and HL7 affiliates ... define identifier systems that SHALL be used for certain types of identifiers.

facts.note: The computable type did not change; the risk comes from local conformance text.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both versions use the same element id and path, `Identifier.system`; only local semantic text changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: There is no cardinality, datatype, regex, or invariant change, so generic StructureDefinition validation may still accept values that satisfy the `uri` primitive. However, the R6 definition and comment narrow conformance expectations: relative/local namespaces and ad hoc systems for identifiers that have registered canonical systems may be rejected by stricter validators, IGs, trading-partner rules, or human conformance review. This is a practical migration risk because identifier matching depends heavily on stable, canonical `system` values.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect or non-canonical identifier systems can cause false matches, missed matches, duplicate records, or rejected claims/transactions when partners expect registered systems.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve interoperability by making identifier namespaces globally unambiguous and aligning known identifier types with registered canonical systems.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4's broader `URL` wording while adding preferred or SHOULD-level guidance for absolute and registered systems.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal is important because `Identifier.system` defines token identity; relative, local, or non-canonical namespaces can undermine matching and interoperability. Making the base text say `absolute URL` and adding registry SHALL guidance is therefore probably reasonable, even though the local evidence does not include the referenced registry page and no computable invariant was added. The less-breaking path is only partial because it would preserve more R4-era local practice at the cost of continuing ambiguity where base R6 is trying to standardize identifier systems.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep the R4-compatible definition (`a URL`) and add text that absolute, registry-defined systems are preferred or SHOULD be used when available. That would reduce conformance pressure on existing local or relative `system` values. It would not fully achieve the R6 goal, however, because relying on softer base language or profile-specific enforcement would leave canonical identifier-system use inconsistent across implementations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves local namespace conventions but weakens global token identity and partner matching consistency.

evidence.detail: R4 says `Identifier.system` establishes a namespace that is `a URL`.
evidence.quote: a URL that describes a set values that are unique

evidence.detail: R6 changes the definition to `an absolute URL`.
evidence.quote: an absolute URL that describes a set values that are unique

evidence.detail: R6 adds SHALL-level guidance to use systems defined by FHIR, THO, or HL7 affiliates for certain identifier types.
evidence.quote: define identifier systems that SHALL be used for certain types of identifiers

examples.examplesMd: The `local-mrn` fragment illustrates a relative/local namespace that may pass weak R4 JSON validation but conflicts with R6's absolute-URL wording. The migrated example uses a stable absolute URL; real migrations should use the jurisdictional or HL7-registered system when one exists.

findings.narrativeMd: `Identifier.system` did not change shape: it is still optional and still has type `uri`. The important change is semantic. R6 says the namespace is an `absolute URL` and adds that FHIR, THO, and HL7 affiliates define systems that SHALL be used for certain identifier types. Systems that historically used local tokens, relative URI references, or home-grown systems where a registered system exists may not see a schema error, but they can fail conformance review or partner validation and can undermine matching behavior.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Generic validation against the core StructureDefinition may not reject all non-absolute or non-registry values because no new invariant or regex was added. The break is therefore potential and policy-dependent: stricter validators, profiles, or trading partners can treat non-absolute or non-registered systems as non-conformant in R6. R6-to-R4 representation is not a structural problem because R4 can carry the same string value in `system`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory `Identifier.system` values. Replace local or relative namespaces with stable absolute URLs, preferably the identifier system URL from the FHIR/THO/affiliate registry when applicable. Regression-test matching, deduplication, token search, and downstream routing because changing `system` values can alter token identity even when `value` is unchanged. Where historical values cannot be rewritten, preserve provenance and document crosswalks from old local systems to canonical systems.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same goal could have been approached with profile-specific requirements or a warning invariant, but base-level text is a defensible interoperability choice because `Identifier.system` is foundational to token identity across all resources. The tradeoff is that old local practices become visibly non-conformant even without a computable validation error.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The local package did not include the referenced `identifier-registry.html` page, so reviewers should confirm which identifier types have mandatory registered systems before classifying partner-specific data as non-conformant.

findings.title: Identifier.use binding updates to the R6 IdentifierUse value set and changes the meaning of `usual`

oldState.summary: R4 `Identifier.use` has a required binding to `identifier-use|4.0.1`; `usual` meant the identifier recommended for display and use in real-world interactions.

binding.description: Identifies the purpose for this identifier, if known .

flags.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not mistake a temporary id for a permanent one.

semanticText.short: usual | official | temp | secondary | old (If known)
semanticText.comment: Applications can assume that an identifier is permanent unless it explicitly says that it is temporary.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4's required code set included `usual`, `official`, `temp`, `secondary`, and `old`. The R4 definition of `usual` was broad: recommended for display and use in real-world interactions.

newState.summary: R6 `Identifier.use` has a required binding to `identifier-use|6.0.0-ballot4`; the code list is unchanged, but `usual` is more specific.

binding.description: Identifies the purpose for this identifier, if known .

changedCodes.oldMeaning: The identifier recommended for display and use in real-world interactions.
changedCodes.newMeaning: The identifier recommended for display and use in real-world interactions which should be used when such identifier is different from the "official" identifier.
changedCodes.changeSummary: R6 clarifies or narrows `usual` to the display/use identifier when it differs from `official`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 and R6 IdentifierUse CodeSystems are complete and contain the same five codes. Only the definition of `usual` changed materially.

flags.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not mistake a temporary id for a permanent one.

semanticText.short: usual | official | temp | secondary | old (If known)
semanticText.comment: Applications can assume that an identifier is permanent unless it explicitly says that it is temporary.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same required code set but updates the bound value-set version and changes the CodeSystem definition of `usual` to emphasize use when the user-facing identifier differs from the official identifier.

facts.note: No required-binding code was added or removed.

facts.oldValue: The identifier recommended for display and use in real-world interactions.
facts.newValue: The identifier recommended for display and use in real-world interactions which should be used when such identifier is different from the "official" identifier.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same `Identifier.use` element and same `http://hl7.org/fhir/identifier-use` CodeSystem were compared. Both CodeSystems declare complete content.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the required code set did not add or remove codes, existing R4 instances using `Identifier.use` codes remain valid against the R6 required binding. The risk is semantic and runtime: decision logic that used `usual` as simply the preferred display identifier may need to account for the explicit relationship to `official`, especially when both are present.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect display or selection of identifiers can cause workflow confusion, but the code-set stability makes a broad validation failure unlikely.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify when `usual` should be used relative to `official` identifiers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No backward-compatible base alternative is needed because the required code set is unchanged and R4 code values remain valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying when `usual` should be used relative to `official` is a reasonable terminology maintenance goal, and the level of breakage is low: no `Identifier.use` code was added or removed, the binding strength did not increase, and R4 instances using the existing codes remain code-valid in R6. The change can still affect business logic that embedded the older definition, so `Probably justified` is more appropriate than treating it as a purely mechanical version update.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue for instance validity because the complete IdentifierUse code set is stable across the two packages. Leaving the R4 definition unchanged and adding explanatory prose elsewhere would avoid semantic drift, but that is not a backward-compatible alternative to a code-set break; it would simply decline the R6 clarification.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Not applicable; implementers may still need to review display and selection semantics for `usual` versus `official`.

evidence.detail: R4 definition of `usual` is broad display/use guidance.
evidence.quote: The identifier recommended for display and use in real-world interactions.

evidence.detail: R6 definition of `usual` adds the condition that it should be used when different from `official`.
evidence.quote: which should be used when such identifier is different from the "official" identifier

examples.examplesMd: The example shows the R6 interpretation where `usual` is the identifier preferred for display/use when it differs from the official identifier. Existing R4 data with only `usual` remains code-valid, but business rules may need review.

findings.narrativeMd: `Identifier.use` remains a required-bound modifier code with the same five codes. The material change is not validation but meaning: R6 updates the value-set version and changes the definition of `usual` so it is specifically the real-world display/use identifier when different from the `official` identifier. Applications that rank identifiers for display, patient lookup, printing, or claim submission should not assume `usual` and `official` are interchangeable.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4 instance becomes invalid solely because of this binding update: the codes are unchanged and the binding strength remains required. R6 instances using the same codes are representable in R4. Runtime risk arises in enum documentation, generated terminology metadata, switch statements with embedded definitions, and business rules that infer priority among `usual`, `official`, and `temp`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Refresh generated terminology artifacts and documentation for `IdentifierUse`. Add tests for resources containing both `official` and `usual` identifiers and confirm display/selection logic chooses the intended identifier. No code-value transform is needed unless local business rules encoded an interpretation of `usual` inconsistent with the R6 definition.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This was largely backward compatible because no code was removed and no binding strength was increased. The same clarification could have been left as narrative-only guidance, but changing the CodeSystem definition is the right place if the intended meaning of a required code has evolved.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, status, kind, type, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. The baseDefinition changed from `Element` to `DataType`, but that is explicitly treated as an out-of-scope base/class-hierarchy issue.
The local Identifier element ids are unchanged: root, `use`, `type`, `system`, `value`, `period`, and `assigner`. No local element was added, removed, renamed, split, or moved.
All local cardinalities are stable: root `0..*` and each local child `0..1`.
Local element datatypes are unchanged: `use` code, `type` CodeableConcept, `system` uri, `value` string, `period` Period, and `assigner` Reference.
`Identifier.assigner` remains `Reference(Organization)` with the same target profile.

Binding strengths are unchanged: `Identifier.use` remains required and `Identifier.type` remains extensible. `Identifier.use` has a finding because the bound version and `usual` definition changed. `Identifier.type` has the same included code list locally, but full R6 THO v2-0203 semantics were not available in the core package.
No local fixed, pattern, or default values were found in either version.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex constraints were added to Identifier's local elements.
`Identifier.use` remains the only local modifier element, with the same modifier reason.
Local summary flags are stable: `use`, `type`, `system`, `value`, `period`, and `assigner` remain summary elements.
No local Identifier-owned slicing was added or changed. Inherited extension slicing is out of scope.
No local serialization representation, choice-name, or element-name change was found for Identifier-owned elements. Inherited `id` XML attribute details are out of scope.

R6 adds no local element or type that R4 cannot carry. R6-to-R4 risk is semantic rather than structural: R4 can represent the same Identifier fields but may not communicate the same warning or updated terminology definitions.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds check-digit guidance to the root Identifier comment
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The new comment says the rules of `identifier.type` determine whether a check digit is part of `Identifier.value` or sent separately, such as through the checkDigit extension. This adds modeling guidance but no cardinality, datatype, or validation requirement.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers with check-digit handling should review whether their `type` coding and extensions reflect R6 guidance, but existing instances are not structurally invalidated by this comment.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Rendered-value extension reference is canonicalized
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 and R6 comments both allow a human display value through a rendered-value extension. R6 changes the reference from a local `extension-rendered-value.html` link to the canonical extension URL/build page. No element shape or requirement changed.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and generated hyperlinks may need refresh, but no data transform is implied solely by this link change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Identifier.type ValueSet metadata changed while local code list stayed the same
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Identifier.type` remains an extensible binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/identifier-type`, and the local ValueSet compose includes the same 18 v2-0203 codes in R4 and R6. The R6 ValueSet metadata changes name/publisher and its narrative references an external THO version, but no local Identifier binding strength or included-code list changed.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Refresh terminology metadata and verify displays/definitions against the R6 ballot's THO dependency if applications rely on code descriptions rather than just codes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 introduces `DataType` as the baseDefinition for `Identifier` whereas R4 specialized `Element` directly. Any codegen or class-hierarchy break from that shift belongs in the `DataType`/base datatype report, not this local Identifier report.

`Identifier.type` uses selected v2-0203 codes. The local R6 core package does not include the external THO CodeSystem, so a terminology-focused comparison should verify displays, definitions, deprecations, and version-specific semantics.

R6 `Identifier.system` points to registry rules and says certain identifier systems SHALL be used. The referenced registry should be reviewed to identify exact systems affected by that conformance text.

analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official HL7 diff/change history and any related ballot issue resolutions for Identifier.
